ordered_diagnoses: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle

s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Symmetric frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth
Normal magnetic resonance imaging of temporal bones and internal auditory canals

shortlist: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle

shortlist.label: Congenital Lower Lip Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the patient's presentation of right lower lip deviation when smiling or crying

shortlist.label: Asymmetric crying face syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by asymmetric facial movement, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the patient's unilateral lower lip weakness

shortlist.label: Moebius Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely given the patient's normal neurodevelopmental examination, it remains a possible diagnosis due to the facial asymmetry

shortlist.label: Isolated Unilateral Congenital Facial Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: A plausible diagnosis given the patient's unilateral facial weakness

raw.rationale: The key fact that the right lower lip deviates inward when the child smiles or cries, but the rest of facial movement is symmetric, is most consistent with Asymmetric crying face syndrome, which is characterized by an abnormal appearance of the mouth when crying due to a weakness of the depressor anguli oris muscle on one side.

rejected.label: Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle
rejected.why: While possible, it is less specific than Asymmetric crying face syndrome

rejected.label: Moebius Syndrome
rejected.why: Typically involves bilateral facial weakness and other cranial nerve palsies, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Isolated Unilateral Congenital Facial Palsy
rejected.why: Would typically involve more extensive facial weakness than just the lower lip

gold: congenital unilateral hypoplasia of depressor anguli oris
